newsitem.title: USA: Duckwall-ALCO says focusing on same-store sales.
newsitem.headline: Duckwall-ALCO says focusing on same-store sales.

text.p: Duckwall-ALCO Stores Inc said on Monday it is continuing to focus on improving same-store sales, which fell four percent in the third quarter this year versus the year-earlier period.

"In spite of declines in same-store sales, we have been able to achieve better than 18 percent growth in net income through improvements in our gross margins and managing our expense growth," said Glen Shank, president and chief executive officer in an earnings statement. "We remain focused on improving same store sales, but not at a cost of buying unprofitable volume increases."
The company reported third quarter net income per share rose to $0.17 from $0.15 with net sales up 6.7 percent at $64.9 million versus $60.8 million in the 1995 third quarter.

It said third quarter same-store sales fell to $54.5 million from $56.8 million in the year-ago period, although net sales for third quarter this year rose 6.7 percent to $64.9 million compared to $60.8 million in the third quarter last year.
The company has 181 retail stores in the central United States. Its shares closed on Friday at $13.
